subject: Pilot cost gate & evaluation roadmap — tokens/$ sensitivity and batching assumptions
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@acmehealth.com>, acme-pm@acmehealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot cost gate & evaluation roadmap — tokens/$ sensitivity and batching assumptions

Karen —

Following our roadmap call this morning, attaching a condensed mutual action plan (MAP) and the pilot economics spreadsheet (attachment: 20280530-acme-pilot-econ-sheet.xlsx). The goal of this thread is to lock the financial gate for the pilot so procurement can confirm the commitment and we can start environment provisioning next week. High-level asks below: 

- Confirm acceptance of the MAP milestones (see section 2 of the PDF) by EOD Tue (06/05).
- Approve the token unit economics assumptions (tokens/$) and indicate any internal rates you want us to use instead of the baseline.
- Confirm whether your security team will require encrypted KV caching at rest (that affects our recommended caching layer).

Key assumptions called out in the econ sheet: 
- Baseline model: small-llama-70B.q4f (Redwood-verified latency profile).
- Avg prompt length: 420 tokens; avg generated tokens: 60 tokens per request.
- Expected concurrency: 5 sustained QPS for demo traffic, spike to 20 QPS during batch ingestion window.
- Caching: prefix KV caching for repeated system prompts and common user prompts — we model 12% token savings at steady state and 28% for warm traffic.
- Batching policy: adaptive batching with 40ms max queue delay; we estimate 18% throughput improvement for long-context requests under this policy.

From those assumptions the pilot TCO delta is shown across three scenarios (pessimistic / baseline / optimistic) in the sheet. Short note on sensitivity: tokens/$ moves non-linearly with cache hit-rate; improving cache hit-rate from 12% to 28% reduces per-request token spend by ~17% in our model.

Attachments: 20280530-acme-pilot-econ-sheet.xlsx (calc tabs: assumptions, sensitivity, per-route breakdown), redwood-map-draft-v2.pdf (MAP milestones + owners).

I expect Marissa to propose a simplified acceptance checklist targeted for procurement; Jordan will walk through the traffic-profile assumptions. If we can get a confirmed econ baseline by Tue, we can keep the original provisioning timeline.

Thanks,
Rishi
--

From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@acmehealth.com>

Cc: acme-pm@acmehealth.com, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cost gate & evaluation roadmap — tokens/$ sensitivity and batching assumptions

Thanks Rishi — quick read-through and a few clarifying questions from our side: 

1) Can you call out the tokens/$ number you used for the baseline (I couldn't find a single-line summary on the PDF)?
2) For caching, does the model require any client-side changes (we prefer server-side transparent caching if possible)?
3) During the demo spike (20 QPS), what fallback policy do you recommend if Dedicated capacity is exhausted? We want to avoid noisy failures during clinical demos.

Also, legal asked if the MAP will include a 10% buffer in committed capacity vs. expected spikes — is that something Redwood typically includes as part of the pilot commitment?

Karen
Karen Liu
Head of Data Platforms | Acme Health
karen.liu@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@acmehealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 May 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cost gate & evaluation roadmap — tokens/$ sensitivity and batching assumptions

Karen — quick answers and an updated econ note inline. I also attached a one-page acceptance checklist (see redwood-map-draft-v2.pdf, page 3) for procurement.

1) Baseline tokens/$: we used $0.019 per 1k generation tokens and $0.0045 per 1k prompt tokens in the baseline calc (tab: assumptions). For the per-request split we modeled 60 gen tokens and 420 prompt tokens which yields a blended tokens/$ of ~ $0.0094 per request at baseline (before cache).

2) Caching: transparent server-side prefix/KV caching is standard for the pilot. No client changes required. The only optional integration is a short-lived cache key that ties to user session for personalization — we can leave that out for the pilot. If you later require client-side hashing to dedupe specific prompts we can add it in a follow-up.

3) Demo spike fallback: our recommended policy is "regional fallback" to a warm compatible model variant (small-llama-70B -> small-llama-70B-quant) with throttled response streaming (we buffer and emit tokens at a controlled rate). That keeps the experience online but with slightly higher latency. We will include automatic fallback in the MAP as milestone 3.2.

4) Committed buffer: yes — we normally include a 10% buffer on reserved pilot capacity for demo-critical windows. We show the buffer as a line-item in the econ sheet under sensitivity (it increases committed cost by ~10–12% depending on the occupancy profile).

Next steps: 
- Karen: confirm you are comfortable with the baseline tokens/$ or provide your preferred internal rates so we can regenerate the sensitivity table.
- Acme: legal/procurement to confirm whether 10% buffer is acceptable or requires additional approvals.
- Rishi/Jordan: we will run one more set of scenario sims (fast/steady/warm) and post updated sheet by Mon 06/03.

Tessa: looping you for the MAP milestone owners and the acceptance checklist details.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Jun 2028 15:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cost gate & evaluation roadmap — tokens/$ sensitivity and batching assumptions

Karen — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Marissa's note we uploaded two items to the shared Drive and pushed an updated calc (link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AcmePilotEcon). Quick summary of the revised numbers after we ran the warm-traffic sim: 

- Baseline blended tokens/$ per request (no cache): $0.0094
- Warm-traffic cache hit-rate: 28% -> blended tokens/$ per request (net): $0.0078 (~17% reduction)
- With 10% committed buffer the monthly reserved cost is estimated at $14,900 (baseline seat + buffer); without buffer $13,500.
- Adaptive batching at 40ms queue cap yields ~15% lower GPU-hours for request mix; we model a 3–5% latency increase on the 95th percentile in exchange.

Action items now: 
- Karen: please confirm by EOD Wed (06/04) whether Acme accepts the baseline tokens/$ and the 10% buffer; that will allow procurement to issue the PO to hit provisioning on 06/10.
- Jordan: finalize the traffic sim tab and snapshot the warm-run by Tue morning.
- Tessa: prep the PO-ready MAP PDF (include the fallback policy language and buffer clause) — loop in legal if they need specific wording.

If Karen confirms, we keep to the pilot close timeline and Redwood will commit to the fall-through fallback and monitoring hooks called out in the MAP.

Thanks —
Rishi
